title_ar: الشيخ محمد الحسن ..يحاضر عن القيم الخلقية في المصارف الإسلامية
title_en: Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Lectures on Moral Values in Islamic Financial Houses
body_ar:
ألقى فضيلة الشيخ محمد الحسن ولد الددو المشرف العام على مركز شنقيط للمالية الإسلامية اليوم الإثنين 13-05-2013 محاضرة حول القيم الخلقية في المصارف الإسلامية، وقد استعرض الشيخ مكانة الأخلاق في الإسلام حيث طفحت الآيات القرآنية والأحاديث النبوية بالإشادة بالخلق والتأكيد عليه مؤكدا أنه لم تقم حضارة ولا بناء بشري إلا على أسا س هذه القيمة وحتى الجاهلية لديهم أخلا ق يتفقون عليها وكانت محل مدح واستحسان ، وجا ء الإسلام فهذبها ووجهها وأودعها مضامين ومفاهيم تسمو بالإنسان وترفع من قدره.

وأكد فضيلة الشيخ أن هذه الأخلاق من ميراث النبوءة الذي يلزم كل مسلم أن يكون له منه حظ و نصيب ، وهي كذلك الضامن لأي نجاح في مسؤولية يتقلدها الإنسان فالتواضع والحلم والجود واللين أخلاق لا يستغني عنها من يتولى ولا ية أو القيام على أسرة أو إدارة مؤسسة.

ونبه فضيلة الشيخ أن خلق الوفاء والصدق والأمانة هي الضامن الوحيد لبناء الثقة والمصداقية فعلى المؤسسات أن لا تعلن عن مشاريع غير حقيقية ولا خدمات غير موجودة ، فالإخلال بالوعد و الالتزامات غير مقبول لسرعة التعامل اليوم، فالتأخير عن سداد مبلغ مثلا بدقائق أصبح مؤثرا، لأن عجلة التنمية تسير بوتيرة وسرعة فائقة، والدقة في المواعيد والإلتزامات أهم عنصر في بناء الثقة ونجاح المؤسسات.

وقد ذكر الشيخ محمد الحسن قواعد أساسية لنجاح أي مشروع اقتصادي استوحاها من حديث عثمان رضي الله عنه ونصيحة قوم قارون،فهذان النصان يعتبران دستورا ووثيقة أخلاقية،يقوم عليهما أي مشروع اقتصادي سليم.

ومن هذه القواعد ،"المعالجة؛ التنمية" ، الاهتمام بالربح تجنب القديم من البضاعة ، فاقد الصلاحية ، اعتماد سياسة عدم وضع البيض في سلة واحدة ، أي تفتيت رأس المال ، وكذلك ابتغاء الدار الآخرة في أي عمل والإحسان وعدم بغي الفساد في الأرض ، وهو معنى شامل يدخل فيه ، بيع الرديء والتزوير والاحتكار وأخذ الديون التي لا يمكن سدادها ، فكل ذلك داخل في مسمى "الإفساد في الأرض".

وختم الشيخ بأن الاقتصاد سلم ترقى عليه الثقافة والحضارة ، لذا ينبغي أن يخلوَ من كل غش وخيانة، وخديعة .

وبعد ذلك رد الشيخ على أسئلة الحضور ، التي كانت لصيقة بموضوع المعاملات والمصارف الإسلامية . والصيغ البديلة عن المعاملات التقليدية.

جدير بالذكر أن هذه المحاضرة أقيمت بفندق اطفيلة بالعاصمة الموريتانية انواكشوط ، ضمن فعاليات الدورة التكوينية التي ينظمها : مركز شنقيط للمالية الإسلامية التابع لجامعة عبد الله ابن ياسين بالتعاون مع بنك المعاملات الصحيحة.

وكان الشيخ الددو المشرف العام على مركز شنقيط للمالية الإسلامية، ألقى كلمة في الجلسة الافتتاحية للدورة أمس .

للمتابعة اضغــط هــنا ...
body_en:
His Eminence Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan Ould al-Dedew, general supervisor of the Shinqit Centre for Islamic Finance, delivered today, Monday 13-05-2013, a lecture on moral values in Islamic financial houses. The Sheikh reviewed the standing of moral character in Islam, in that the Qur'anic verses and the prophetic reports overflow with the commendation of character and with emphasis upon it, affirming that no civilisation and no human structure has ever stood except upon the basis of this value; and that even the people of the age of ignorance (jāhiliyyah) had moral standards they agreed upon, which were an object of praise and approval — and Islam came and refined them, gave them direction, and placed in them contents and conceptions that elevate the human being and raise his worth.

His Eminence the Sheikh affirmed that these moral standards are part of the inheritance of prophethood, of which every Muslim is bound to have a portion and a share, and that they are likewise what guarantees any success in a responsibility a person takes on: humility, forbearance, generosity and gentleness are moral qualities that cannot be dispensed with by anyone who assumes an office, or takes charge of a family, or manages an institution.

His Eminence the Sheikh cautioned that the character of fidelity, truthfulness and trustworthiness (amānah) is the only guarantee for the building of confidence and credibility. Institutions must not announce projects that are not real, nor services that do not exist. Breaching a promise and one's undertakings is not acceptable, given the speed of dealing today: being minutes late in settling a sum, for example, has become consequential, because the wheel of development turns at an extraordinary pace and speed, and precision in appointments and undertakings is the most important element in building confidence and in the success of institutions.

Sheikh Muhammad al-Hasan mentioned basic rules for the success of any economic undertaking, which he drew from the report of Uthman (may God be pleased with him) and from the counsel of Qarun's people — for these two texts are to be regarded as a constitution and a moral charter upon which any sound economic undertaking rests.

Among these rules: 'treatment; development'; attention to profit; avoiding old stock and goods past their validity; adopting the policy of not putting the eggs in one basket, that is, of breaking up capital; and likewise seeking the abode of the hereafter in any work, and doing good, and not seeking corruption in the earth — which is a comprehensive sense that takes in the selling of defective goods, falsification, hoarding, and taking on debts that cannot be repaid, for all of that falls under the name of 'corruption in the earth'.

The Sheikh closed by saying that the economy is a ladder by which culture and civilisation ascend, and that it must therefore be free of every kind of cheating, betrayal and deception.

After that the Sheikh answered the questions of those present, which were closely tied to the subject of transactions (muʿāmalāt) and Islamic financial houses, and of the alternative forms to conventional transactions.

It is worth noting that this lecture was held at the Tfeila Hotel in the Mauritanian capital Nouakchott, within the proceedings of the training course organised by the Shinqit Centre for Islamic Finance, attached to Abdullah ibn Yasin University, in cooperation with the Bank of Sound Transactions.

Sheikh al-Dedew, general supervisor of the Shinqit Centre for Islamic Finance, had delivered an address at the opening session of the course yesterday.

flags.arabic: "المعالجة؛ التنمية" ، الاهتمام بالربح تجنب القديم من البضاعة ، فاقد الصلاحية
flags.context: the opening of the list of rules for a successful economic undertaking
options: 'treatment; development'; attention to profit; avoiding old stock and goods past their validity
'processing and development'; concern for profit; avoiding old and expired stock
the list is corrupt and should not be translated as a list
flags.note: SOURCE DEFECT (house rule 11) and a genuine uncertainty. The list is garbled: 'المعالجة؛ التنمية' stands in quotation marks with no verb and no context, the punctuation between the items is inconsistent, and 'فاقد الصلاحية' floats without an obvious head noun. The items have been rendered individually and in the source's order without inventing connectives. This list should not be presented as the Sheikh's own scheme of rules until it is checked against the lecture recording.

flags.arabic: حديث عثمان رضي الله عنه ونصيحة قوم قارون
flags.context: the two texts from which the Sheikh drew his rules
options: the report of Uthman (may God be pleased with him) and the counsel of Qarun's people
the ḥadīth concerning Uthman and the advice given to Qarun by his people
flags.note: 'نصيحة قوم قارون' is the counsel given to Qarun in Sūrat al-Qaṣaṣ 28:77 ({ seek, by means of what God has given you, the abode of the hereafter… and do not seek corruption in the earth }), which the later paragraph then paraphrases. 'حديث عثمان' is unidentified: the source gives no collection, no wording and no grading, and it is not clear whether a prophetic report transmitted by Uthman or a saying of his own is meant. Nothing has been supplied (style guide §4). A reviewer should identify the text before publication.

flags.context: the co-organiser of the training course
flags.note: Same Mauritanian bank as in article 817, where it appears as 'بنك المعاملات الصحيحة الإسلامي'. Rendered literally and consistently across both records; the bank's own registered name should replace this once confirmed. See also 'فندق اطفيلة', the Tfeila Hotel in Nouakchott, whose Latin spelling is taken from the hotel's own usage.

flags.context: وأكد فضيلة الشيخ أن هذه الأخلاق من ميراث النبوءة
options: part of the inheritance of prophethood
part of the legacy of prophecy
flags.note: The source writes 'النبوءة' (prophecy, in the sense of foretelling) where 'النبوّة' (prophethood, the office) is meant; the two are distinguished in Arabic and the reporter has used the wrong one. Translated by the evident sense and flagged.

translator_notes: News summary of a lecture. No legal ruling is given anywhere in the text — the content is moral exhortation applied to banking practice, and nothing here should be rendered with the five rulings. 'المصارف' rendered 'financial houses' and 'البنوك' 'banks' consistently with article 817. Source defects preserved in body_ar: stray spaces inside words ('أسا س', 'أخلا ق', 'وجا ء', 'ولا ية'), missing spaces after commas, and 'النبوءة' for 'النبوّة'. CMS date is a bulk-upload timestamp, not a composition date.
